title: Safety Review: Ownership Checklist
story: The borrow checker is XIOM's most famous feature — and the most feared by newcomers. But it operates on simple rules. Learn the rules, and the compiler becomes your ally instead of your adversary.
why: A systematic ownership audit catches use-after-move, double-borrow, and lifetime violations at the design stage, before you even compile.
analogy: The ownership rules are like traffic laws — they feel restrictive until you realize they're the only thing preventing head-on collisions.
try_it: Trace `main()` line by line. At each line, answer: who owns `res`? When is `&mut res` borrowed and released? When does `res` move into `consume_resource`? Could you call `process_resource(&mut res)` after `consume_resource(res)`? Why not?
tips: The compiler IS your checklist — every borrow error is one of the 5 rules being violated
When you get a borrow error, identify which rule is broken, then fix the design, not just the syntax
Practice tracing ownership on paper until it becomes mental — it's the fastest way to fluency
common_mistakes: Trying to beat the borrow checker with unsafe — the checker is right 99.9% of the time; your 'clever' workaround is wrong
Using clone() to silence borrow errors — understand WHY the error occurred before reaching for clone
Returning references to local variables — the variable dies when the function returns; the reference becomes dangling
